BASIC PROTOCOL
A high-resolution BN-PAGE followed by in-gel activity of the mitochondrial complexes is an efficient and easy approach to determine the stoichiometry of the SCs, as opposed to highly specialized mass spectrometric methods. In contrast to sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS)-
PAGE, BN-PAGE allows protein separation under native conditions and preserves protein-
protein interactions, which is important for studying SCs. Following solubilization of mitochondria and centrifugation, the anionic dye Coomassie G-250 sample additive is added to the supernatant. This dye is sufficiently soluble in water, but it can also bind to membrane proteins because of its hydrophobic properties. Binding a large number of dye molecules imposes a charge shift on the proteins that causes even basic proteins to migrate to the anode at pH 7.5 during the electrophoresis step of BN-PAGE. Here, proteins are not separated according to the charge/mass ratio but according to size in acrylamide gradient gels. Protein migration gradually decelerates with running distance and with decreasing pore size of the gradient gel. Individual proteins stop migrating almost completely when they approach their size-dependent specific pore-size limit during BN-PAGE. Because negatively charged protein surfaces repel each other, the tendency of membrane proteins to aggregate is considerably reduced. Furthermore, membrane surfaces lose their hydrophobic character upon binding the dye, which converts membrane proteins into water-soluble proteins. This means that no detergent is required in the BN gels once Coomassie dye has occupied the protein surfaces. Therefore, the risk of denaturation of detergent-sensitive proteins is minimized during BN-PAGE (Wittig et al., 2007).
Here, we describe a high-throughput method for resolving SCs and assessing their activity. This protocol will guide researchers through the two broad steps involved in mitochondrial SC visualization/analysis (see Figure 2 for a scheme).
STEP 1. Mitochondria isolation from mouse liver (applies for others organs as well)
MATERIALS—Mouse tissue ~30 mg liver. ~ 15 mg is sufficient for organs with high mitochondrial content (e.g. brain and heart).

METHOD
1. Sacrifice a mouse under anesthesia (e.g. 3-5% isoflurane (Adams and Pacharinsak, 2015)) and excise the liver, rinse the liver briefly with ice-cold IB, excise and put about 30 mg of liver tissue into an ice-cold Wheaton Glass tube (appropriate for 2-
ml homogenization volume).
Note 1: Snap frozen tissues that are appropriately stored can also be used with this protocol. Freezing does not affect the activity of the SCs.
2. Add 2 ml of ice-cold IB into the Wheaton glass tube, homogenize the liver at 1500 rpm (or max. speed). For liver, 20 strokes are required. Increase the number of strokes if the tissue is not homogenized well. For cells (primary or cultured), ~40 strokes will be required.
Note 2: Keep the homogenizer probe under the surface of IB to avoid foaming.
3. Transfer 2 ml of the homogenate into a 2-ml Eppendorf tube and centrifuge at 600 × g for 10 min at 4°C. This step will separate the cell debris from the mitochondrial extract.
4. Transfer the supernatant (about 1.5 ml, leave the supernatant which is close to the pellet to avoid contamination) to a 1.5 ml tube and centrifuge at 7,000 × g for 10 min at 4°C. Discard the supernatant and resuspend the pellet (which is the mitochondria) in 2ml of cold IB by tapping the tube. Centrifuge again at 7,000 × g for 10 min at 4°C.
5. Decant the supernatant and resuspend the pellet in ~0.25 ml of cold IB. This volume can be changed depending on the pellet size. Care should be taken not to dissolve the pellet in too much IB, which would impact the protein determination.
ALTERNATIVE PROTOCOL: The pellet (mitochondria) from step 5 can be stored at −80°C after the removal of the supernatant. Frozen mitochondria can be stored at −80°C for yrs. Alternatively, the resuspended mitochondria from step 5 can also be frozen and stored at −80°C for several months for later use. Although 1-2 cycles of freezing-thawing of the resuspended mitochondrial extract does not affect the quality of the BN-PAGE and immunoblotting, it is always better to make aliquots of the extract before storage.
6. Measure the mitochondrial protein concentration from the above resuspended pellet (to determine the mitochondrial protein content) using the Bradford Jha et al. Page 4

Figure 1. Schematic representation of the oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) system showing its individual complexes, supercomplexes and its nomenclature
(A) Mitochondrial electron transport chain (ETC) and ATP synthesis. In TCA cycle, NADH and succinate are electron donors, oxidized by NADH dehydrogenase (CI) and succinate dehydrogenase (CII), respectively. Ubiquinone (Q) is one of the electron acceptors which transfers the electrons to cytochrome c (c) by cytochrome c reductase (CIII). The electrons then pass to their terminal acceptor molecular oxygen (O2) to release water by cytochrome c oxidase (CIV). This electron transfer is coupled with the transfer of protons (H+) across mitochondrial inner membrane, except complex II. The electrochemical proton gradient generated drives the generation of chemical energy in the form of adenosine triphosphate (ATP) through ATP synthase (CV). Note that in this figure, for simplicity, all components are shown as monomers, however in reality their stoichiometry is more complex e.g. complex III exists as dimers (as shown in the figure). steps.title: Prepare all reagents and solutions
steps.instruction: Make the following solutions using Milli‑Q water: EGTA/Tris 0.1 M (3.8 g EGTA in 50 ml water, adjust pH to 7.4 with Tris, bring to 100 ml, store 4 °C, 1 yr); Isolation buffer (6.846 g sucrose, 0.121 g Tris, 1 ml 0.1 M EGTA/Tris in 80 ml water, adjust pH to 7.4 with 1 M HEPES, bring to 100 ml, store –20 °C, 6 mo, add 1× protease inhibitor fresh before use); Native PAGE anode buffer (add 50 ml 20× buffer to 950 ml water for 1 L); Dark blue cathode buffer (dissolve 0.044 g Coomassie Brilliant Blue G‑250 in 220 ml Native PAGE anode buffer); Light blue cathode buffer (mix 20 ml dark blue buffer with 180 ml Native PAGE anode buffer, use once); Transfer buffer (as supplied with iBlot); Blocking solution (10 ml: 2 ml Blocker/Diluent A + 3 ml Blocker/Diluent B + 5 ml water); Primary antibody solution (10 ml: 2 ml Blocker/Diluent A + 1 ml Blocker/Diluent B + 10 µl anti‑OXPHOS cocktail + 5 µl anti‑MTCO1 antibody + 7 ml water); Antibody wash solution (5 ml 16× diluted with 75 ml water); Chromogenic substrate solution (as supplied); Activity substrates prepared fresh: • Complex I (20 ml water + 40 µl 1 M Tris‑HCl pH 7.4, 2 mg NADH, 50 mg NTB); • Complex IV (100 ml: 50 mg DAB, 100 mg cytochrome c, 90 ml 50 mM phosphate pH 7.4, bring to 100 ml, aliquot 10–15 ml, store –20 °C); • Complex II (10 ml: 200 µl 1 M sodium succinate, 25 mg NTB, 8 µl 250 mM phenazine methosulphate in DMSO, 50 µl 1 M Tris‑HCl pH 7.4, water to 9.742 ml); • Complex V (10 ml: 350 µl 1 M Tris, 2.7 ml 1 M glycine, 140 µl 1 M MgSO₄, 100 µl 1 M ATP, 20 mg Pb(NO₃)₂, water to 6.710 ml).

steps.title: Solubilize mitochondria on ice
steps.instruction: Add digitonin to the isolated mitochondrial pellet to achieve the desired digitonin‑to‑protein ratio (e.g., 8 g digitonin per g protein or 4 g/g as indicated later) and mix gently; incubate the solubilized mitochondria on ice for 20 min, avoiding bubble formation.

steps.title: Clarify solubilized mitochondria
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the solubilized mitochondria at 20 000 × g for 10 min at 4 °C; carefully transfer 15 µl of the supernatant to a fresh tube.

steps.title: Add Coomassie G‑250 sample additive
steps.instruction: Add 2 µl of Coomassie Brilliant Blue G‑250 sample additive to the 15 µl supernatant so that the final G‑250 concentration equals one‑quarter of the detergent concentration; add immediately before loading the gel.

steps.title: Assemble BN‑PAGE gel and apparatus
steps.instruction: Remove the white tape from the bottom of a NativePAGE 3–12 % gradient gel, place the gel into the XCell SureLock Mini‑Cell apparatus.

steps.title: Pre‑wash gel wells with dark blue buffer
steps.instruction: Wash each well with 1 ml dark blue cathode buffer; fill the inner chamber with 20 ml dark blue cathode buffer and check for leakage.

steps.title: Load samples and run BN‑PAGE
steps.instruction: Load 15 µl of each prepared sample into the wells using Prot/Elec tips; fill the inner chamber with ~180 ml dark blue cathode buffer and the outer chamber with ~600 ml running buffer; run at 150 V for 30 min. Then remove the dark blue buffer with a 10‑ml pipette or suction, fill the inner chamber with 200 ml light blue cathode buffer, and continue running at 250 V for 60 min (up to 150 min if higher resolution is required).

substeps.instruction: If in‑gel activity is planned, modify the second voltage step as described in STEP 2 (B).

steps.title: Transfer proteins to PVDF membrane
steps.instruction: Remove the gel from the cassette, rinse briefly with water, then incubate the gel in transfer buffer for 15 min with gentle shaking.

steps.title: Set up iBlot transfer
steps.instruction: Attach the sponge to the lid of the iBlot Transfer Device; place the anode stack (PVDF membrane on top) at the bottom, carefully lay the gel onto the membrane, remove bubbles with the provided roller, pre‑wet a filter paper with transfer buffer and place it onto the gel, add the cathode stack with the rough side up, close the lid and select program 3 (7 min) to start transfer.

steps.title: Fix and wash membrane after transfer
steps.instruction: After transfer, remove the PVDF membrane, incubate in 8 % acetic acid for 5 min with gentle shaking, wash twice with water for 5 min each, then air‑dry the membrane by clipping one side.

steps.title: Remove Coomassie from membrane
steps.instruction: Incubate the membrane in 100 % methanol for 5 min, repeat two more times with gentle shaking; wash the membrane three times with water for 5 min each.

steps.title: Block membrane
steps.instruction: Incubate the membrane with 10 ml blocking solution for 30 min at 21 °C with gentle shaking; during this incubation prepare the primary antibody solution; afterwards wash the membrane twice with water for 5 min each.

steps.title: Incubate with primary antibody
steps.instruction: Incubate the membrane with 10 ml primary antibody solution for 90 min at 21 °C with gentle shaking; prepare the antibody wash solution while incubating.

steps.title: Wash after primary antibody
steps.instruction: Wash the membrane twice with 10 ml antibody wash solution for 5 min each with gentle shaking, then wash twice with water for 5 min each.

steps.title: Incubate with secondary antibody
steps.instruction: Incubate the membrane with 10 ml secondary antibody solution for 45 min at 21 °C with gentle shaking.

steps.title: Wash after secondary antibody
steps.instruction: Wash twice with 10 ml antibody wash solution for 5 min each with gentle shaking, then wash twice with water for 5 min each.

steps.title: Chromogenic detection and imaging
steps.instruction: Incubate the membrane with chromogenic substrate solution while shaking until the expected bands become clear (typically 3–10 min, maximum 60 min); stop the reaction by replacing the solution with water, wash twice with water for 5 min each, air‑dry the membrane and scan the image.

steps.title: Adjust digitonin‑protein ratio and run time (optional note)
steps.instruction: For a digitonin‑to‑protein ratio of 8 g/g run the gel 30 min at 150 V followed by 90 min at 250 V; for a ratio of 4 g/g run 30 min at 150 V followed by 150 min at 250 V, as illustrated in Figures 3 and 4G.

steps.title: Prepare samples for Clear‑Native (CN)‑PAGE
steps.instruction: Prepare the sample buffer cocktail as described in STEP 2 (A) point 8; add 20 µl of this buffer to 50 µg mitochondrial protein, mix gently with a 20 µl pipette, and incubate on ice for 20 min.

steps.title: Clarify CN‑PAGE samples
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 20 000 × g for 10 min at 4 °C; collect 15 µl supernatant and add 2 µl Coomassie G‑250 additive (final concentration 1/4 of detergent).

steps.title: Assemble CN‑PAGE gel and light blue buffer
steps.instruction: Set up the XCell SureLock Mini‑Cell as for BN‑PAGE; dissolve 0.022 g Coomassie Brilliant Blue G‑250 in 200 ml Native PAGE anode buffer to make light blue cathode buffer; wash gel wells with 1 ml light blue buffer, fill the inner chamber with 20 ml light blue buffer and check for leakage.

steps.title: Load and run CN‑PAGE
steps.instruction: Load 15 µl of each sample, fill the inner chamber with ~180 ml light blue cathode buffer and the outer chamber with ~600 ml running buffer; run at 150 V for 30 min, then replace the light blue buffer with clear cathode/running buffer and continue at 250 V for an additional 150 min (total 180 min) for optimal supercomplex separation.

steps.title: In‑gel activity assays (CN‑PAGE)
steps.instruction:
After electrophoresis, place the gel in ice‑cold water. Then perform the following assays (use 50 µg liver protein unless otherwise noted):
• Complex I: incubate gel in 20 ml Complex I substrate for 15–20 min (violet bands); stop with 10 % acetic acid, wash, and scan.
• Complex IV: incubate gel in 20 ml Complex IV substrate for 30–40 min (brown bands); stop with 10 % acetic acid, wash, and scan.
• Complex IV + I: first incubate in Complex IV substrate until brown signal appears, wash ~1 min with water, then incubate in Complex I substrate until blue signal appears; stop with 10 % acetic acid, wash, and scan.
• Complex II: incubate gel in 10 ml Complex II substrate for ~40 min (violet bands); stop with 10 % acetic acid, wash, and scan.
• Complex V: incubate gel in 10 ml Complex V substrate overnight (~16 h) (transparent/silver bands); stop with 50 % methanol, wash, scan, and invert the scanned image to view bands.
• Complex III: detect by immunoblotting (see STEP 3).

steps.title: Optional Coomassie staining of BN‑PAGE gel
steps.instruction: If immunoblotting is not required, stain the BN‑PAGE gel with a colloidal blue staining kit using ~100–150 µg protein (higher protein improves SC visualization); destain as described in the kit.
